A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LayerAvatar and retain matching methods and experiments. All supplied pages, figures, tables and equations support comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains supplementary Sections 6–8.

before.justification: v1 reports original avatar-generation results on TightCap and THuman2.0, quantitative ablations in Table 2, and qualitative animation and component-transfer results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds user-study results, disentanglement measurements, robustness tests and supplementary reconstruction experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the three-layer Gaussian UV representation, shared geometry/texture decoders, SMPL-X deformation, joint fitting/diffusion training and existing loss terms. The supplement supplies implementation details and additional applications without documenting a revised core algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 retains TightCap and THuman2.0 and adds composite training data from THuman2.0, THuman2.1 and CustomHuman, with demonstrations of more varied clothing including dresses and skirts. Supplementary experiments add single-image reconstruction on unseen 4DDress, noisy-mask scenarios and multi-layer outfit composition, substantially extending the represented data and task conditions.

E2.justification: SO-SMPL, LAGA and TELA become evaluated comparators in Table 1c and Figure 3; v1 only cites these works. Conversely, EG3D is removed from both dataset comparisons and PrimDiff from the THuman2.0 comparison. EVA3D, Rodin, HumanLiff, StructLDM and E3Gen remain in their respective comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces masked inter-layer L-PSNR, a 20-participant preference study, and reconstruction experiments comparing UV resolutions 128/256 and decoder depths two/three using PSNR. It also adds a 1,954-scan composite-data experiment. The original THuman2.0 setting of 500 scans/54 views and TightCap setting of 107 samples/158 views remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original two-stage, SLMO and SLMN ablations are retained. Section 8.2 adds TV-loss removal, sensitivity to single-view versus persistent multi-view mask noise, feature-resolution/decoder-depth ablations, controlled body-shape examples and unseen-dataset reconstruction demonstrations. These substantially broaden analysis of component behavior, robustness and generalization.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's participant count and preference scores introduce an evaluation design and outcomes, without adding an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Retained FIDs remain 17.37 on TightCap and 12.50 on THuman2.0, and Table 2 is unchanged. New results include L-PSNR above 40 versus HumanLiff's 28.57, preference and timing results in Table 1c, and reconstruction PSNRs of 38.08, 38.55 and 37.34 for the three configurations in Figure O. Supplementary qualitative findings are added, while EG3D/PrimDiff result entries are removed. These are additional results, not improvements to the retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The representation, rendering, deformation and training mathematics in Equations 1–12 remain substantively unchanged. Initial-value notation and scale/rotation wording are corrected, and the v-prediction explanation is shortened, without changing the mathematical reasoning. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion replace the categorical 'first' claim with 'novel.' The front matter also drops explicit 1024-resolution and real-time-rendering claims while emphasizing generation detail. The central claims of component disentanglement, layered representation, efficient generation and component transfer remain.

C2.justification: Unlike v1, Section 8.1 explicitly discusses segmentation/SMPL-X errors, body–clothing collisions, loose-clothing animation artifacts, accessory coverage and missing physical constraints. Section 8.2 attributes noise tolerance to multi-view supervision and discusses texture imbalance and limited poses as quality constraints. These materially clarify applicability and failure conditions.

D1.justification: Section 7 newly specifies feature-plane dimensions, decoder/U-Net configurations, initialization, learning rates, loss weights, batch/view sampling, six-day training on two RTX 3090 GPUs, and data preprocessing. These are disclosures rather than evidence of changed existing settings. One ambiguity remains: Section 3.2 calls the decoders MLPs, whereas Figure G describes convolutional blocks.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting datasets, metrics, implementation, additional avatar work and possible extensions, including CustomHuman, HumanNeRF and GarmageNet. The related-work categories and distinction from entangled or optimization-based generation remain largely intact, while replacing 'first' with 'novel' narrows the priority positioning.

P1.justification: The five-section main-text structure and much of the prose remain. Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, representation explanation and conclusion; Section 4 gains explicit baseline and metric paragraphs. Author information is updated, and new supplementary sections organize implementation details and discussions.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes three separate comparison panels, and the main qualitative comparison is substantially reorganized and expanded. v2 adds an E3Gen close-up comparison, architecture diagrams, a configuration table and supplementary experimental figures. v1's standalone template and expressive-animation figures are omitted, while existing ablation and component-transfer displays are reordered or revised.

improvement.justification: v1 provides limited implementation information and largely visual evidence specifically addressing disentanglement. v2 substantially strengthens these areas through L-PSNR and component-focused comparisons, targeted robustness analyses, detailed implementation disclosures and explicit limitations in Sections 7–8. The user-study protocol remains sparsely documented and decoder descriptions are inconsistent, but the gains in evidential support, reproducibility information and qualification of claims clearly outweigh these shortcomings.
